test_title: PYST 62: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 13 Nov, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5
solution:
The correct answer is '**practice**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage describes how Orson Welles, the director of 'Citizen Kane', broke with traditional filmmaking conventions.
 
• The blank refers to a conventional method or custom that Hollywood traditionally followed.
 
• "**Practice**" fits perfectly, as it means the actual application or use of an idea, belief, or method. It refers to a standard procedure or a routine way of doing something. In this case, the standard Hollywood procedure was to maintain a careful appearance for the heroine.
 
• Other options do not fit the context: "**practicals**" refers to practical examinations or things you do in practice, which doesn't fit the context; "**prose**" refers to written or spoken language in its ordinary form, which is irrelevant; and "**practise**" is the verb form (British English), but a noun is needed here.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel **truth__* *that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a **__blow__* *at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which **__permeated__* *every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful **__eye__* *on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this **__practice __****in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Practicals: (usually plural) a practical exam or lesson.
 
• Prose: written or spoken language in its ordinary form, without metrical structure.
 
• Practise: (verb) to perform an activity or exercise repeatedly or regularly in order to improve or maintain one's proficiency. (British English)
